and judging how probability statements in the media should influence our decisions.","family":"data","section":{"no":5,"name":"Data Handling and Probability","strand":"Making Sense of and Using Data","from":16,"to":20},"outcomes":["Identify uses of probability in print and electronic media and in Ghanaian institutions.","Interpret probability statements correctly and explain common misunderstandings.","Calculate experimental probabilities from data and compare them with theoretical probabilities.","Convert between probabilities, percentages and betting odds, and recognise a bookmaker’s margin.","Distinguish relative from absolute risk and use expected value to judge raffles, bets and insurance.","Explain how a probability statement should, and should not, influence an individual decision."],"keywords":["probability","probability scale","event","outcome","theoretical probability","experimental probability","relative frequency","forecast","risk","relative risk","absolute risk","effectiveness","odds","implied probability","margin","expected value","fair game","insurance","poll","margin of error","gambler’s fallacy","misconception"],"notes":[{"title":"The probability scale","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The **probability** of an event is a number from 0 to 1 (or 0% to 100%) measuring how likely it is."},{"k":"fig","id":"w19-scale","caption":"From impossible to certain."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Two ways to find a probability","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Theoretical** (equally likely outcomes): $P(A)=\\dfrac{\\text{number of favourable outcomes}}{\\text{number of possible outcomes}}$.","**Experimental** (relative frequency): $P(A)\\approx\\dfrac{\\text{number of times }A\\text{ happened}}{\\text{number of trials}}$.","$P(\\text{not }A)=1-P(A)$.","Expected number of times $A$ occurs in $n$ trials $=n\\times P(A)$."]}]},{"k":"p","text":"The more trials, the closer the relative frequency usually comes to the true probability (Figure 19.2). It means that in conditions like these, rain fell on about 70 days out of 100.","**A 70% chance of winning is not a guarantee.** In 10 such matches the team is expected to win about 7 and lose or draw about 3.","**“87% effective”** means the vaccinated group’s risk is 87% lower than the unvaccinated group’s, not that 87 of every 100 doses work.","**The gambler’s fallacy:** past results do not change the probability of independent events. Good reports give both."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w19-risk","caption":"A 90% relative reduction in risk."}],"figs":["w19-risk"]},{"title":"Odds and betting","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Bookmakers quote **decimal odds**: a stake of GH₵1 at odds of 2.10 returns GH₵2.10 (the stake plus GH₵1.10 profit) if the bet wins."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Odds and expected value","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Implied probability $=\\dfrac{1}{\\text{decimal odds}}$. The implied probabilities of all outcomes add up to **more than 1**: the excess is the bookmaker’s **margin**, which guarantees the bookmaker a profit in the long run.","**Expected value** of a game: multiply each outcome’s value by its probability and add, $E=\\sum x\\,P(x)$. A game is **fair** if the expected gain is 0. Raffles, lotteries and bets have a **negative** expected value for the player."]}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w19-odds","caption":"Implied probabilities add up to more than 1."},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Making decisions with probability","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A probability is information, not an instruction. Combine it with the **consequences**: a 30% chance of rain may not stop a football match, but a 30% chance of flooding near a riverside school should trigger preparation. A smart decision weighs both the chance and the cost of being wrong, and checks the source and the sample behind the number."}]}],"figs":["w19-odds"]}],"examples":[{"title":"A rain forecast","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The Ghana Meteorological Agency reports a 65% probability of rain in Accra tomorrow. (d) Find the probability that it does not rain."}],"steps":["(a) That it will rain over 65% of Accra, or for 65% of the day; or that rain is certain and only the timing is unknown.","(b) On past days with similar conditions it rained on about 65 days in every 100.","(c) A student carries an umbrella and leaves early; a farmer may delay spraying or irrigating; a driver checks tyres and wipers and expects slower traffic.","(d) $1-0.65=0.35$."],"answer":"(b) rain on about 65 of 100 such days (d) 0.35","figs":[]},{"title":"Vaccine effectiveness","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A study finds that a flu vaccine is 87% effective. A forecast is judged over many predictions, not one.","(d) Fans may feel confident; some bettors back Medeama, others back the opponent hoping for an upset at bigger odds."],"answer":"(b) 14 (c) not necessarily","figs":[]},{"title":"Relative and absolute risk","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A headline says: “Eating food fried in reused oil doubles your risk of a rare stomach illness!” The risk rises from 1 in 10 000 to 2 in 10 000 people per year. (c) What should a careful reader do?"}],"steps":["(a) Relative increase $=\\dfrac{2-1}{1}\\times100\\%=100\\%$ (“doubles”). Find the expected gain on a GH₵10 bet on Hearts."}],"steps":["(a) $\\dfrac{1}{2.10}\\approx0.476$, $\\dfrac{1}{3.20}\\approx0.313$, $\\dfrac{1}{3.50}\\approx0.286$; total $\\approx1.074$.","(b) The extra 0.074 (7.4%) is the bookmaker’s margin: the odds are set below fair values so that the bookmaker profits over many bets.","(c) Win: return GH₵21 (gain GH₵11) with probability 0.443; lose GH₵10 with probability 0.557.","Expected gain $=0.443\\times11-0.557\\times10=4.87-5.57\\approx-0.70$: on average the bettor loses about 70 pesewas per GH₵10."],"answer":"(a) 0.476, 0.313, 0.286; total 1.074 (c) about −GH₵0.70","figs":[]},{"title":"Is the raffle worth it?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A school sells 2000 raffle tickets at GH₵5 each. The prizes are one of GH₵2000, four of GH₵500 and twenty of GH₵50. (a) Find the probability that a ticket wins a prize. (b) Find the expected value of the prizes per ticket. (c) Find the expected gain of buying one ticket. (d) Why is the raffle still acceptable as a fund-raiser?"}],"steps":["(a) $\\dfrac{1+4+20}{2000}=\\dfrac{25}{2000}=0.0125$.","(b) Total prizes $=2000+2000+1000=5000$; per ticket $\\dfrac{5000}{2000}=2.50$, that is GH₵2.50.","(c) $2.50-5=-2.50$: an expected loss of GH₵2.50 per ticket.","(d) Buyers knowingly donate to the school; the expected loss is the donation, and the school raises GH₵10 000 − GH₵5000 = GH₵5000."],"answer":"(a) 0.0125 (b) GH₵2.50 (c) −GH₵2.50","figs":[]},{"title":"Setting an insurance premium","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"An insurer estimates that the probability of a particular motorbike being stolen in a year is 0.02. (c) Why does insurance make sense for the owner even though the expected value is negative?"}],"steps":["(a) $0.02\\times15\\,000=300$, that is GH₵300.","(b) GH₵300 covers expected claims; GH₵150 covers administration, staff and profit.","(c) A loss of GH₵15 000 would be a disaster for the owner, while GH₵450 is affordable. Insurance spreads the cost of rare large losses over many people."],"answer":"(a) GH₵300 (b) GH₵150 for costs and profit","figs":[]},{"title":"Lending and default risk","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A microfinance company estimates a 30% chance that a new borrower will not repay. (c) What interest rate is this? (d) Comment on fairness."}],"steps":["(a) $200\\times0.3=60$ defaults, so 140 repay.","(b) $\\dfrac{200\\,000}{140}\\approx1428.57$, that is about GH₵1428.57 each.","(c) About 42.9% interest just to break even, before any costs or profit.","(d) Honest borrowers pay for defaulters; better checks on borrowers (lowering the default probability) would allow lower interest rates."],"answer":"(a) 60 (b) about GH₵1428.57 (c) about 42.9%","figs":[]},{"title":"An opinion poll","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A poll of 1000 voters in a region gives Candidate A 52% and Candidate B 48%, with a margin of error of ±3 percentage points. (c) How might such a statement affect voters?"}],"steps":["(a) A: 49% to 55%; B: 45% to 51%.","(b) No. The ranges overlap, so B could actually be ahead; the race is too close to call.","(c) Supporters of A may stay at home thinking the result is decided, while B’s supporters may work harder: polls can change behaviour."],"answer":"(a) 49–55% and 45–51% (b) no: too close to call","figs":[]},{"title":"The gambler’s fallacy","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) A coin has shown heads five times in a row. (c) A lottery player always avoids last week’s numbers. Skipping it is a high-risk strategy.","(c) No. Every set of numbers has the same chance in each draw."],"answer":"(a) no (b) not a safe inference (c) no","figs":[]},{"title":"Probabilities from weather data","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The illustrative monthly data show rainfall (mm) and mean temperature (°C) for a town in southern Ghana. Taking each month as equally likely: (a) find P(low temperature) (b) find P(heavy rainfall) (c) find P(low temperature and heavy rainfall) (d) find P(low temperature, given heavy rainfall) (e) explain (c) to a layperson."}],"steps":["(a) Low temperatures in June, July, August, September and October: $P=\\dfrac{5}{12}$.","(b) Heavy rain in April, May, June, September and October: $P=\\dfrac{5}{12}$.","(c) Both in June, September and October: $P=\\dfrac{3}{12}=\\dfrac14$.","(d) Of the 5 heavy-rain months, 3 are cool: $\\dfrac35$.","(e) “In about one month out of every four, it is both cooler than usual and very rainy, so plan for both together then.” Note the data are monthly averages for one location and may differ from year to year."],"answer":"(a) $\\tfrac{5}{12}$ (b) $\\tfrac{5}{12}$ (c) $\\tfrac14$ (d) $\\tfrac35$","figs":["w19-weather"]},{"title":"Bed nets and malaria","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A district report says: “Of 1500 children who did not sleep under treated nets, 120 had malaria last year; of 1000 who did, 40 had malaria.” (a) Find the experimental probability of malaria in each group. What else would you want to know?"}],"steps":["(a) Without nets: $\\dfrac{120}{1500}=0.08$ (8%). With nets: $\\dfrac{40}{1000}=0.04$ (4%).","(b) Absolute reduction 4 percentage points; relative reduction $\\dfrac{8-4}{8}=50\\%$.","(c) “Halves” matches these figures, but this is observational: families who use nets may also live in better housing or nearer clinics. Ask how children were chosen, whether other factors were similar, and whether the result is repeated in other districts. For each: (a) write the statement and source (b) explain its meaning simply (c) give two common misconceptions (d) give three real-life effects on decisions. Then answer: (e) Why should the media explain probabilities clearly? (f) How can schools reduce misunderstanding?","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"A good answer gives full statements with source and date, for example “There is an 80% chance of rain in Accra tomorrow” (GMet, accessed on a stated date); a plain explanation (“on 80 of 100 similar days, it rained”); misconceptions (rain for 80% of the day; rain is certain); effects (carry umbrellas, postpone outdoor events, farmers delay spraying)."},{"k":"p","text":"(e) Because people act on these numbers; unclear statements lead to poor decisions, panic or complacency."},{"k":"p","text":"(f) Teach probability through real forecasts, health and sport examples; practise converting between percentages, fractions, odds and expected numbers; and discuss absolute versus relative risk."}]},{"q":"A health campaign says a new malaria vaccine is 75% effective. Unvaccinated: $4800\\times0.2=960$. Total $1320$: about 1080 cases prevented."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) Absolute risk 5% (down from 20%, a fall of 15 points); relative reduction 75%."},{"k":"p","text":"(d) “In our district about 1 child in 5 gets malaria each year. It does not give complete protection, so keep sleeping under treated nets, but vaccinating most children could prevent around a thousand cases a year.”"}]},{"q":"A betting company offers the following odds for a match: Team P win 1.70, draw 3.60, Team Q win 5.50. (d) Explain, using expected value, why betting is not a way to make money in the long run, and give one social effect of heavy betting among young people.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) $\\tfrac{1}{1.70}\\approx0.588$, $\\tfrac{1}{3.60}\\approx0.278$, $\\tfrac{1}{5.50}\\approx0.182$; total $\\approx1.048$, a margin of about 4.8%."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) Divide each by 1.048: about 0.561, 0.265 and 0.174."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) Win: gain $20\\times4.5=90$ with probability 0.174; lose 20 with probability 0.826. Expected gain $\\approx15.66-16.52=-0.86$, a loss of about GH₵0.86."},{"k":"p","text":"(d) Because the odds include the bookmaker’s margin, every bet has a negative expected value: over many bets the bettor loses about the margin on each cedi staked. (a) Find the probability that a flood in this district occurs in June. (b) Find the experimental probability that a given year has a flood in June, if June floods occurred in 14 of the 40 years. (c) How should NADMO use this information? (d) State two limitations of using past data to predict floods.","steps":[],"answer":"","model":[{"k":"p","text":"(a) Total floods $=2+6+14+5+3+8+2=40$; $P(\\text{June}\\mid\\text{flood})=\\tfrac{14}{40}=0.35$."},{"k":"p","text":"(b) $\\tfrac{14}{40}=0.35$ per year."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) Pre-position boats, food and medicine and clear drains before June and October, and run evacuation drills in the most flood-prone areas."},{"k":"p","text":"(d) Climate change and new building on flood plains may make the past a poor guide; 40 years is a limited record, and recording methods may have changed."}]},{"q":"(a) Explain the difference between theoretical and experimental probability, with an example of each. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y3w20">{"year":3,"week":20,"id":"y3w20","title":"Probability II: Dependent and Independent Events","subtitle":"Solving everyday problems involving two or more events, using the multiplication and addition laws; independent, dependent and mutually exclusive events; conditional probability; drawing with and without replacement; tree diagrams, two-way tables and area models; problems with cards, dice, contracts, committees and medical tests.","family":"data","section":{"no":5,"name":"Data Handling and Probability","strand":"Making Sense of and Using Data","from":16,"to":20},"outcomes":["Distinguish between independent, dependent and mutually exclusive events and give real-life examples of each.","Use the multiplication law, including the conditional form P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B|A).","Use the addition law P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).","Solve problems on drawing with and without replacement, including cards and beads.","Use tree diagrams, two-way tables and the complement to find “exactly one” and “at least one” probabilities.","Find and interpret conditional probabilities in real-life contexts such as screening tests."],"keywords":["experiment","trial","outcome","sample space","event","complement","independent events","dependent events","mutually exclusive","conditional probability","multiplication law","addition law","with replacement","without replacement","tree diagram","two-way table","at least one","exactly one"],"notes":[{"title":"Key terms","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"The language of probability","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["An **experiment** is a planned activity with a well-defined set of possible outcomes, for example tossing a coin or drawing a card. Each performance is a **trial**.","The **sample space** $S$ is the set of all possible outcomes; an **event** $E$ is a subset of $S$.","For equally likely outcomes, $P(E)=\\dfrac{n(E)}{n(S)}$ and $0\\le P(E)\\le1$.","The **complement** $E'$ is “$E$ does not happen”: $P(E')=1-P(E)$."]}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Three kinds of pairs of events","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Independent:** one event does not change the chance of the other. *Examples:* tossing a coin and rolling a die; drawing **with** replacement.","**Dependent:** the first event changes the chance of the second. *Examples:* drawing **without** replacement; choosing a committee or officers.","**Mutually exclusive:** the events cannot happen together. *Example:* one card being both an ace and a six."]},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Conditional probability and the multiplication law","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The probability of $A$ given that $B$ has happened is"},{"k":"math","tex":"P(A\\mid B)=\\frac{P(A\\cap B)}{P(B)},\\qquad P(B)>0."},{"k":"p","text":"So $P(A\\cap B)=P(B)\\times P(A\\mid B)=P(A)\\times P(B\\mid A)$."},{"k":"ul","items":["$A$ and $B$ are **independent** exactly when $P(A\\mid B)=P(A)$, that is, when $P(A\\cap B)=P(A)\\times P(B)$.","If $A$ and $B$ are **mutually exclusive**, $P(A\\cap B)=0$."]}]},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"The addition law","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"P(A\\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\\cap B)."},{"k":"p","text":"For mutually exclusive events this becomes $P(A\\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w20-venn","caption":"Why the overlap is subtracted."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"“And” multiplies, “or” adds","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["“$A$ **and then** $B$”: multiply along the branch, using the probability of $B$ **after** $A$ has happened.","“$A$ **or** $B$” for different routes that cannot both happen: add the routes.","“**Exactly one**”: add both orders, $A$ then not-$B$ and not-$A$ then $B$.","“**At least one**”: use $1-P(\\text{none})$."]}]}],"figs":["w20-venn"]},{"title":"With and without replacement","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"When an item is drawn and **put back**, the sample space is the same for every draw, so the draws are independent. When it is **not put back**, each draw changes both the total and the count of that kind, so the draws are dependent."},{"k":"fig","id":"w20-beads","caption":"The second draw has a new sample space."}],"figs":["w20-beads"]},{"title":"A standard pack of cards","blocks":[{"k":"fig","id":"w20-deck","caption":"52 cards: 4 suits of 13 ranks."},{"k":"box","kind":"note","title":"Facts about the pack","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["4 suits of 13 cards: hearts and diamonds are red; spades and clubs are black, so 26 red and 26 black.","Each rank (Ace, 2, …, 10, Jack, Queen, King) has 4 cards.","12 **picture** (face) cards: the Jack, Queen and King of each suit.","The number cards 2 to 10 make 36 cards; 20 of them are even (2, 4, 6, 8, 10). If the Ace is counted as 1, then 20 cards are odd (A, 3, 5, 7, 9); if not, 16 are odd. Always state which convention you use."]}]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Common errors","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Mutually exclusive is not the same as independent.** If $P(A)>0$ and $P(B)>0$ and they cannot happen together, then knowing $A$ happened makes $P(B)=0$, so they are dependent.","**$P(A\\mid B)$ is not $P(B\\mid A)$.** The probability that a person with malaria tests positive is not the probability that a person who tests positive has malaria.","Forgetting to reduce **both** the total and the count after a draw without replacement.","Counting only one order when the question says “in any order” or “one of each”."]}]},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Probability at work","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Banks multiply default probabilities across loans, clinics use conditional probability to interpret test results, contractors estimate the chance of winning several bids, and sports analysts model penalty shoot-outs as chains of dependent events."}]}],"figs":["w20-deck"]}],"examples":[{"title":"Repeated independent trials","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A social media quiz app gives a 30% chance of winning a prize on each spin, independently. (a) Find the probability of winning on both of two spins. (b) Find the probability of at least one win in two spins. (c) Find the least number of spins needed for the probability of at least one win to exceed 0.9."}],"steps":["(a) $0.3\\times0.3=0.09$, that is 9%.","(b) $P(\\text{no win in 2})=0.7^2=0.49$, so $P(\\text{at least one})=1-0.49=0.51$.","(c) We need $1-0.7^n>0.9$, so $0.7^n<0.1$.","Taking logs: $n\\log0.7<\\log0.1$. Since $\\log0.7<0$, the inequality reverses: $n>\\dfrac{\\log0.1}{\\log0.7}\\approx6.46$.","So $n=7$ spins. Check: $0.7^6\\approx0.118$ and $0.7^7\\approx0.082$."],"answer":"(a) 0.09 (b) 0.51 (c) 7 spins","figs":[]},{"title":"Beads without replacement","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A box contains 5 red and 3 green beads. Kojo draws two beads at random without replacement. Find the probability that (a) the first is red and the second is green (b) both are green (c) the beads are of different colours (d) at least one bead is green."}],"steps":["(a) $P(R_1)=\\dfrac58$; then 7 beads remain, 3 green: $P(G_2\\mid R_1)=\\dfrac37$. So $\\dfrac58\\times\\dfrac37=\\dfrac{15}{56}$.","(b) $\\dfrac38\\times\\dfrac27=\\dfrac{6}{56}=\\dfrac{3}{28}$.","(c) Red then green, or green then red: $\\dfrac{15}{56}+\\dfrac38\\times\\dfrac57=\\dfrac{15}{56}+\\dfrac{15}{56}=\\dfrac{30}{56}=\\dfrac{15}{28}$.","(d) $P(\\text{no green})=\\dfrac58\\times\\dfrac47=\\dfrac{20}{56}$, so $P(\\text{at least one green})=1-\\dfrac{20}{56}=\\dfrac{36}{56}=\\dfrac{9}{14}$.","Check: $20+15+15+6=56$, so the four branches add up to 1."],"answer":"(a) $\\tfrac{15}{56}$ (b) $\\tfrac{3}{28}$ (c) $\\tfrac{15}{28}$ (d) $\\tfrac{9}{14}$","figs":["w20-tree"]},{"title":"With or without replacement?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"For the same box of 5 red and 3 green beads, find the probability that both beads are green when the first bead is replaced before the second draw. The probability that he wins X is 0.5, and the probability that he does **not** win Y is 0.3. Find the probability that he wins (a) both contracts (b) exactly one contract (c) neither contract (d) at least one contract."}],"steps":["$P(X)=0.5$, $P(Y)=1-0.3=0.7$.","(a) $P(X\\cap Y)=0.5\\times0.7=0.35$.","(b) $P(X\\text{ only})=0.5\\times0.3=0.15$ and $P(Y\\text{ only})=0.5\\times0.7=0.35$, so exactly one $=0.15+0.35=0.5$.","(c) $0.5\\times0.3=0.15$.","(d) $1-0.15=0.85$. Check: $0.35+0.5+0.15=1$."],"answer":"(a) 0.35 (b) 0.5 (c) 0.15 (d) 0.85","figs":["w20-area"]},{"title":"Two cards without replacement","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Two cards are drawn at random, without replacement, from a standard pack of 52. All 12 picture cards remain among 51: $\\dfrac{12}{51}=\\dfrac4{17}$. So $\\dfrac1{13}\\times\\dfrac4{17}=\\dfrac4{221}$.","(b) $\\dfrac{13}{52}\\times\\dfrac{13}{51}=\\dfrac14\\times\\dfrac{13}{51}=\\dfrac{13}{204}$ (all 13 hearts remain).","(c) 20 even cards: $\\dfrac{20}{52}\\times\\dfrac{19}{51}=\\dfrac{5}{13}\\times\\dfrac{19}{51}=\\dfrac{95}{663}$."],"answer":"(a) $\\tfrac{4}{221}$ (b) $\\tfrac{13}{204}$ (c) $\\tfrac{95}{663}$","figs":[]},{"title":"When the first card overlaps the second event","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Two cards are drawn without replacement. Find the probability of (a) a heart, then a red card (b) a red card, then a heart."}],"steps":["(a) After a heart, 25 red cards remain among 51: $\\dfrac{13}{52}\\times\\dfrac{25}{51}=\\dfrac{325}{2652}=\\dfrac{25}{204}$.","(b) The first red card may or may not be a heart, so split into cases.","First a heart: $\\dfrac{13}{52}\\times\\dfrac{12}{51}=\\dfrac{156}{2652}$. First a diamond: $\\dfrac{13}{52}\\times\\dfrac{13}{51}=\\dfrac{169}{2652}$.","Total: $\\dfrac{156+169}{2652}=\\dfrac{325}{2652}=\\dfrac{25}{204}$.","The two answers agree: both count the same number of ordered pairs (a heart and a red card that is not the same card)."],"answer":"both $\\tfrac{25}{204}$","figs":[]},{"title":"The addition law with two dice","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Two fair dice are thrown. Let $A$ be “the sum is 8” and $B$ be “a double is thrown”. Find (a) $P(A)$ (b) $P(B)$ (c) $P(A\\cap B)$ (d) $P(A\\cup B)$ (e) $P(A\\mid B)$, and state whether $A$ and $B$ are independent."}],"steps":["(a) Sum 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2): $P(A)=\\dfrac5{36}$.","(b) Six doubles: $P(B)=\\dfrac6{36}=\\dfrac16$.","(c) Only (4,4): $P(A\\cap B)=\\dfrac1{36}$.","(d) $\\dfrac5{36}+\\dfrac6{36}-\\dfrac1{36}=\\dfrac{10}{36}=\\dfrac5{18}$.","(e) $P(A\\mid B)=\\dfrac{1/36}{6/36}=\\dfrac16$. Since $\\dfrac16\\ne\\dfrac5{36}$, the events are dependent."],"answer":"(d) $\\tfrac{5}{18}$ (e) $\\tfrac16$; dependent","figs":["w20-dice"]},{"title":"Conditional probability from a two-way table","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A survey of 200 SHS students recorded whether each owns a smartphone."},{"k":"table","head":["","owns phone","no phone","total"],"rows":[["boys","60","30","90"],["girls","66","44","110"],["total","126","74","200"]]},{"k":"p","text":"A student is chosen at random. Find (a) $P(\\text{owns a phone})$ (b) $P(\\text{owns}\\mid\\text{girl})$ (c) $P(\\text{girl}\\mid\\text{owns})$ (d) whether owning a phone is independent of being a girl."}],"steps":["(a) $\\dfrac{126}{200}=0.63$.","(b) Restrict to the 110 girls: $\\dfrac{66}{110}=0.6$.","(c) Restrict to the 126 owners: $\\dfrac{66}{126}=\\dfrac{11}{21}\\approx0.524$.","(d) $P(\\text{owns}\\mid\\text{girl})=0.6\\ne0.63=P(\\text{owns})$, so the events are not independent. Equivalently, $P(\\text{girl}\\cap\\text{owns})=0.33$ while $P(\\text{girl})\\times P(\\text{owns})=0.55\\times0.63\\approx0.347$.","Notice that (b) and (c) are different: conditioning on a different group changes the denominator."],"answer":"(a) 0.63 (b) 0.6 (c) $\\tfrac{11}{21}$ (d) not independent","figs":[]},{"title":"Testing for independence","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(A)=0.4$, $P(B)=0.5$ and $P(A\\cup B)=0.7$. (d) Find $P(A\\mid B')$."}],"steps":["(a) $0.7=0.4+0.5-P(A\\cap B)$, so $P(A\\cap B)=0.2$.","(b) $P(A)\\times P(B)=0.2=P(A\\cap B)$: independent.","(c) No, since $P(A\\cap B)=0.2\\ne0$.","(d) $P(A\\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\\cap B)=0.2$ and $P(B')=0.5$, so $P(A\\mid B')=\\dfrac{0.2}{0.5}=0.4=P(A)$, as expected for independent events."],"answer":"(a) 0.2 (b) yes (c) no (d) 0.4","figs":[]},{"title":"Interpreting a malaria test","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"At a clinic, 10% of patients who come with fever have malaria. Find the probability that the patient has malaria."}],"steps":["Let $M$ be “has malaria” and $T$ be “tests positive”. $P(M)=0.1$, $P(T\\mid M)=0.95$, $P(T\\mid M')=0.04$.","$P(M\\cap T)=0.1\\times0.95=0.095$.","$P(M'\\cap T)=0.9\\times0.04=0.036$.","$P(T)=0.095+0.036=0.131$.","$P(M\\mid T)=\\dfrac{0.095}{0.131}\\approx0.725$.","In 1000 such patients: 95 true positives and 36 false positives, so about 27% of positive results are false. This is why clinicians may confirm a positive result with a second test."],"answer":"about 0.725","figs":[]},{"title":"Choosing two prefects","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A class of 12 boys and 8 girls chooses a prefect and then an assistant prefect at random; one student cannot hold both posts. If the Ace is not counted as a number, there are 16 odd cards: $\\tfrac{16}{52}\\times\\tfrac{15}{51}=\\tfrac{20}{221}$."}]},{"q":"Three boxes A, B and C contain green, yellow and orange balls respectively, all the same size. The ratio of balls in A to B is 3 : 5, and in B to C is 2 : 3. All the balls are poured into one container and mixed. (a) Find the probability of selecting a green ball. (b) Two balls are drawn one after the other with replacement. Find the probability of (i) a yellow and an orange ball, in any order (ii) a yellow ball first, then a green ball. Either order: $2\\times\\tfrac{10}{31}\\times\\tfrac{15}{31}=\\tfrac{300}{961}$."},{"k":"p","text":"(ii) $\\tfrac{10}{31}\\times\\tfrac{6}{31}=\\tfrac{60}{961}$."},{"k":"p","text":"(c) 62 balls is 2 per part: 12 green, 20 yellow, 30 orange. $\\tfrac{30}{62}\\times\\tfrac{29}{61}=\\tfrac{870}{3782}=\\tfrac{435}{1891}\\approx0.230$."}]},{"q":"In a community, 8% of adults have hepatitis B. <script>/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   A small LaTeX reader for the maths used in the planners (Years 1–3), and

   simple HTML for pasting.  The typesetter (layout.js) draws the same tree.

    times: '×', div: '÷', pm: '±', mp: '∓', cdot: '·', ast: '∗', star: '⋆', bullet: '•',
    infty: '∞', circ: '∘', degree: '°', partial: '∂', nabla: '∇',
    ldots: '…', dots: '…', cdots: '⋯', vdots: '⋮', ddots: '⋱',
    Rightarrow: '⇒', Longrightarrow: '⟹', rightarrow: '→', longrightarrow: '⟶', Leftarrow: '⇐', leftarrow: '←', longleftarrow: '⟵',
    Leftrightarrow: '⇔', Longleftrightarrow: '⟺', leftrightarrow: '↔', iff: '⟺', implies: '⟹', impliedby: '⟸', mapsto: '↦', to: '→', gets: '←',
    uparrow: '↑', downarrow: '↓', nearrow: '↗', searrow: '↘',
    therefore: '∴', because: '∵', emptyset: '∅', varnothing: '∅', forall: '∀', exists: '∃', neg: '¬', lnot: '¬',
    wedge: '∧', land: '∧', vee: '∨', lor: '∨', oplus: '⊕', otimes: '⊗',
    lbrace: '{', rbrace: '}', '{': '{', '}': '}', '%': '%', '$': '$', '#': '#', '&': '&', '_': '_',
    lt: '<', gt: '>', vert: '|', lvert: '|', rvert: '|', Vert: '‖', mid: '∣', nmid: '∤', prime: '′', checkmark: '✓',
    triangle: '△', angle: '∠', measuredangle: '∡', square: '□', blacksquare: '■', Box: '□', diamond: '◇',
    perp: '⊥', parallel: '∥', sim: '∼', simeq: '≃', cong: '≅', lfloor: '⌊', rfloor: '⌋', lceil: '⌈', rceil: '⌉',
    langle: '⟨', rangle: '⟩', backslash: '∖', aleph: 'ℵ', ell: 'ℓ', hbar: 'ℏ', dagger: '†'

    iota: 'ι', kappa: 'κ', lambda: 'λ', mu: 'μ', nu: 'ν', xi: 'ξ', pi: 'π', varpi: 'ϖ', rho: 'ρ', varrho: 'ϱ', sigma: 'σ', varsigma: 'ς',
    tau: 'τ', upsilon: 'υ', phi: 'ϕ', varphi: 'φ', chi: 'χ', psi: 'ψ', omega: 'ω',
    Gamma: 'Γ', Delta: 'Δ', Theta: 'Θ', Lambda: 'Λ', Xi: 'Ξ', Pi: 'Π', Sigma: 'Σ', Upsilon: 'Υ', Phi: 'Φ', Psi: 'Ψ', Omega: 'Ω'
  };
  const BIGOP = { sum: '∑', prod: '∏', int: '∫', oint: '∮', bigcup: '⋃', bigcap: '⋂' };
  const FN = ['sin', 'cos', 'tan', 'csc', 'sec', 'cot', 'arcsin', 'arccos', 'arctan', 'sinh', 'cosh', 'tanh', 'log', 'ln', 'lg', 'exp',
    'max', 'min', 'lim', 'det', 'arg', 'deg', 'gcd', 'lcm', 'sup', 'inf', 'dim', 'ker', 'hom', 'Pr'];
  const BB = { N: 'ℕ', Z: 'ℤ', Q: 'ℚ', R: 'ℝ', C: 'ℂ', W: '𝕎', P: 'ℙ' };
  const ACC = { dot: ['̇', 'dot'], ddot: ['̈', 'ddot'], bar: ['̅', 'bar'], overline: ['̅', 'bar'], hat: ['̂', 'hat'], widehat: ['̂', 'hat'],
    vec: ['⃗', 'vec'], overrightarrow: ['⃗', 'arrow'], overleftrightarrow: ['⃡', 'arrow2'], tilde: ['̃', 'tilde'], widetilde: ['̃', 'tilde'],
    underline: ['̲', 'under'], check: ['̌', 'hat'], breve: ['̆', 'hat'], acute: ['́', 'hat'], grave: ['̀', 'hat'] };
  const FRAC = ['frac', 'dfrac', 'tfrac', 'cfrac'];
  const IGNORE = ['displaystyle', 'textstyle', 'scriptstyle', 'limits', 'nolimits', 'big', 'Big', 'bigg', 'Bigg', 'bigl', 'bigr', 'Bigl', 'Bigr', 'biggl', 'biggr',
    'left.', 'right.', 'nonumber', 'notag', 'hline', 'allowbreak', 'strut', 'mathstrut', 'color_'];
  const NOT = { '=': '≠', '∈': '∉', '⊂': '⊄', '⊆': '⊈', '≡': '≢', '∼': '≁', '<': '≮', '>': '≯', '∣': '∤', '≤': '≰', '≥': '≱' };

  function tokenize(s) {
    const out = []; let i = 0;
    while (i < s.length) {
      const c = s[i];
      if (c === '\\') {
        let j = i + 1;
        if (/[A-Za-z]/.test(s[j] || '')) { while (j < s.length && /[A-Za-z]/.test(s[j])) j++; out.push({ k: 'cmd', v: s.slice(i + 1, j) }); i = j; while (s[i] === ' ') i++; continue; }

      }

      const cp = s.codePointAt(i); const ch = String.fromCodePoint(cp);

    }
    return out;
  }

  function parse(src) {
    const t = tokenize(String(src)); let p = 0; const errors = [];
    const peek = () => t[p];
    const skipSp = () => { while (peek() && peek().k === 'sp') p++; };
    function group() {           // {...} or a single atom (one character of a number)
      skipSp();
      const k = peek();
      if (k && k.k === '{') { p++; const n = seq('}'); if (peek() && peek().k === '}') p++; else errors.push('missing }'); return n; }
      if (k && k.k === 'num' && k.v.length > 1) { const first = k.v[0]; t[p] = { k: 'num', v: k.v.slice(1) }; return [{ t: 'run', s: first }]; }

    }
    function optArg() {
      skipSp();
      if (peek() && peek().k === '[') { p++; const n = seq(']'); if (peek() && peek().k === ']') p++; return n; }
      return null;
    }
    function rawText() {        // \text{...}: keep spaces and plain characters
      skipSp();
      if (!(peek() && peek().k === '{')) { const a = t[p++]; return a ? (a.v || '') : ''; }
      p++; let s = ''; let depth = 0;
      while (p < t.length) {
        const k = t[p];
        if (k.k === '}' && depth === 0) { p++; break; }
        if (k.k === '{') depth++; if (k.k === '}') depth--;
        if (k.k === '$') { p++; continue; }
        s += k.k === 'sp' ? ' ' : k.k === 'cmd' ? (SYM[k.v] ?? GREEK[k.v] ?? SPACE[k.v] ?? (k.v === '\\' ? ' ' : '')) : k.k === 'num' || k.k === 'ch' ? (k.v === '−' ? '-' : k.v === '∗' ? '*' : k.v) : (k.k === '{' || k.k === '}' ? '' : k.k);
        p++;
      }
      return s;
    }
    function envName() {
      skipSp(); let name = '';
      if (peek() && peek().k === '{') {
        p++;
        while (p < t.length && t[p].k !== '}') { name += t[p].v || (t[p].k === 'sp' ? '' : ''); p++; }
        p++;
      }
      return name;
    }
    function env(name) {
      const rows = [[]]; let cell = [];
      let guard = 0;
      while (p < t.length && guard++ < 20000) {
        const k = peek();
        if (k.k === '&') { p++; rows[rows.length - 1].push(cell); cell = []; continue; }
        if (k.k === 'cmd' && k.v === '\\') { p++; optArg(); rows[rows.length - 1].push(cell); cell = []; rows.push([]); continue; }
        if (k.k === 'cmd' && k.v === 'end') { p++; envName(); break; }
        if (k.k === 'cmd' && k.v === 'hline') { p++; continue; }
        const n = scripted(); if (n) cell.push(n);
      }
      rows[rows.length - 1].push(cell);
      while (rows.length > 1 && rows[rows.length - 1].every(c => !c.length)) rows.pop();
      const base = name.replace(/\*$/, '');
      const delims = { pmatrix: ['(', ')'], bmatrix: ['[', ']'], Bmatrix: ['{', '}'], vmatrix: ['|', '|'], Vmatrix: ['‖', '‖'], matrix: ['', ''], smallmatrix: ['', ''], cases: ['{', ''], array: ['', ''] };
      if (base === 'aligned' || base === 'align' || base === 'split' || base === 'gathered' || base === 'alignat' || base === 'eqnarray') return { t: 'mat', rows, open: '', close: '', align: base === 'gathered' ? 'c' : 'rl' };
      if (base === 'cases') return { t: 'mat', rows, open: '{', close: '', align: 'l' };
      const d = delims[base] || ['', ''];
      if (!delims[base]) errors.push('env ' + name);
      return { t: 'mat', rows, open: d[0], close: d[1], align: 'c' };
    }
    function atom() {
      const k = t[p++]; if (!k) return null;
      if (k.k === 'sp') return { t: 'run', s: '' };
      if (k.k === 'num') return { t: 'run', s: k.v };
      if (k.k === 'ch') return { t: 'run', s: k.v };
      if (k.k === '[' || k.k === ']') return { t: 'run', s: k.k };
      if (k.k === '&') return { t: 'run', s: '' };
      if (k.k === '{') { const n = seq('}'); if (peek() && peek().k === '}') p++; return { t: 'grp', body: n }; }
      if (k.k === 'cmd') {
        const v = k.v;
        if (FRAC.includes(v)) { const a = group(), b = group(); return { t: 'frac', num: a, den: b, small: v === 'tfrac' }; }
        if (v === 'binom' || v === 'dbinom' || v === 'tbinom') { const a = group(), b = group(); return { t: 'delim', open: '(', close: ')', body: [{ t: 'frac', num: a, den: b, nobar: true }] }; }
        if (v === 'sqrt') { const deg = optArg(); return { t: 'rad', deg, body: group() }; }
        if (ACC[v]) return { t: 'acc', chr: ACC[v][0], kind: ACC[v][1], body: group() };
        if (v === 'mathbb') { const g = group(); const c = g.map(n => n.s || '').join(''); return { t: 'run', s: [...c].map(x => BB[x] || x).join('') }; }
        if (v === 'text' || v === 'mathrm' || v === 'textrm' || v === 'mbox' || v === 'textup' || v === 'operatorname' || v === 'textnormal' || v === 'mathsf' || v === 'textsf') return { t: 'run', s: rawText(), plain: true, fn: v === 'operatorname' };
        if (v === 'textbf' || v === 'mathbf' || v === 'boldsymbol' || v === 'bm') {
          // bold maths: keep maths italics for letters only when \boldsymbol, plain bold for \mathbf/\textbf

        if (v === 'phantom' || v === 'hphantom' || v === 'vphantom') { group(); return { t: 'run', s: '' }; }
        if (v === 'color' || v === 'textcolor') { group(); return v === 'textcolor' ? { t: 'grp', body: group() } : { t: 'run', s: '' }; }
        if (v === 'boxed' || v === 'fbox') return { t: 'grp', body: group() };
        if (v === 'cv') { const a = group(), b = group(); return { t: 'mat', rows: [[a], [b]], open: '(', close: ')', align: 'c' }; }
        if (v === 'begin') { const name = envName(); if (name === 'array') { skipSp(); if (peek() && peek().k === '{') group(); } return env(name); }
        if (v === 'end') { envName(); return { t: 'run', s: '' }; }
        if (v === 'pmod') { const g = group(); return { t: 'grp', body: [{ t: 'run', s: ' (mod ', plain: true }, ...g, { t: 'run', s: ')', plain: true }] }; }
        if (v === 'bmod' || v === 'mod') return { t: 'run', s: ' mod ', plain: true, fn: true };
        if (v === 'xrightarrow' || v === 'xleftarrow' || v === 'overset' || v === 'stackrel') {
          if (v === 'overset' || v === 'stackrel') { const top = group(), base = group(); return { t: 'over', top, body: base }; }
          optArg(); const top = group();
          return { t: 'over', top, body: [{ t: 'run', s: v === 'xrightarrow' ? '⟶' : '⟵' }] };
        }
        if (v === 'underset') { const bot = group(), base = group(); return { t: 'under', bot, body: base }; }
        if (v === 'not') {
          skipSp(); const nx = scripted(); const s = nx && nx.t === 'run' ? nx.s : '';
          return { t: 'run', s: NOT[s] || (s ? s + '̸' : ''), op: true };
        }
        if (v === 'left' || v === 'right') {
          const readDelim = () => {
            skipSp(); const d = t[p++]; let ch = '';
            if (d) {
              if (d.k === 'cmd') ch = SYM[d.v] ?? (d.v === '|' ? '‖' : d.v === '{' ? '{' : d.v === '}' ? '}' : '');
              else if (d.k === 'ch') ch = d.v;
              else if (d.k === '[' || d.k === ']') ch = d.k;
              else if (d.k === 'num' && d.v[0] === '.') { ch = ''; if (d.v.length > 1) { p--; t[p] = { k: 'num', v: d.v.slice(1) }; } }
            }
            return ch;
          };
          const ch = readDelim();
          if (v === 'right') return { t: 'run', s: ch };          // a stray \right
          const body = []; let close = '';
          while (p < t.length) {
            if (peek().k === 'cmd' && peek().v === 'right') { p++; close = readDelim(); break; }
            const n = scripted(); if (!n) break; body.push(n);
          }
          return { t: 'delim', open: ch, close, body };
        }
        if (FN.includes(v)) return { t: 'run', s: v, plain: true, fn: true, lim: v === 'lim' || v === 'max' || v === 'min' };
        if (BIGOP[v]) return { t: 'run', s: BIGOP[v], big: true };
        if (IGNORE.includes(v)) return { t: 'run', s: '' };

          if (n.kind === 'under') return `<m:bar><m:barPr><m:pos m:val="bot"/>${ctrl}</m:barPr>${e('e', n.body)}</m:bar>`;
          if (n.kind === 'arrow' || n.kind === 'arrow2') return `<m:groupChr><m:groupChrPr><m:chr m:val="${n.kind === 'arrow' ? '→' : '↔'}"/><m:pos m:val="top"/><m:vertJc m:val="bot"/>${ctrl}</m:groupChrPr>${e('e', n.body)}</m:groupChr>`;

        case 'frac': { const a = f(n.num), b = f(n.den); const w = x => x.length > 1 && /[+−\-\s]/.test(x) ? `(${x})` : x; return n.nobar ? `${a}, ${b}` : `${w(a)}/${w(b)}`; }

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Planner engine: settings -> class context -> a planner document model.
   The document model is rendered twice: as HTML (preview) and as Word XML.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
const WEEKS = {};

const B = {
  p: (text, o = {}) => ({ k: 'p', text, ...o }),
  h: (text, o = {}) => ({ k: 'h', text, lvl: 1, ...o }),
  h2: (text, o = {}) => ({ k: 'h', text, lvl: 2, ...o }),
  ul: (items, o = {}) => ({ k: 'ul', items: items.filter(Boolean), ...o }),
  ol: (items, o = {}) => ({ k: 'ol', items: items.filter(Boolean), ...o }),
  math: (tex) => ({ k: 'math', tex }),
  fig: (id, caption, cm) => ({ k: 'fig', id, caption, cm }),
  table: (o) => ({ k: 'table', ...o }),
  note: (text, o = {}) => ({ k: 'p', text, note: true, ...o }),
  adapt: (text, o = {}) => ({ k: 'p', text, adapt: true, ...o }),
  // a shaded band that opens each activity: title on the left, time and organisation on the right
  bar: (text, right, o = {}) => ({ k: 'bar', text, right: right || '', keep: true, act: true, ...o }),
  // a small coloured sub-heading inside an activity (Teach, Worked example, Differentiated practice …)
  label: (text, o = {}) => ({ k: 'p', text: `**${text}**`, color: 'accent', size: 9.6, before: 3.5, after: 1, keep: true, label: true, ...o })
};

const NEEDS = {
  visual: 'Low vision / visual impairment',
  hearing: 'Hearing impairment',
  physical: 'Physical disability',
  reading: 'Reading difficulty (dyslexia)',
  attention: 'Attention difficulty (ADHD)',
  language: 'Limited English',
  shy: 'Shy or quiet learners',
  gifted: 'Gifted and talented',
  absent: 'Absentees and latecomers',
  behaviour: 'Learners who lose focus'
};
const RESOURCES = {
  manila: 'Manila card and markers',
  maths_set: 'Mathematical sets',
  calculators: 'Calculators',
  projector: 'Projector and laptop',
  phones: 'Learners’ phones or tablets',
  internet: 'Internet / GeoGebra',
  printer: 'Printer or photocopier',
  slates: 'Mini whiteboards or slates',
  sticky: 'Sticky notes',
  tactile: 'Tactile materials (string, glue)',
  material: 'Learner Material copies',
  tape: 'Masking tape or chalk (floor number line)'
};
const STRATEGIES = {
  problem: 'Problem-based learning',
  talk: 'Think–pair–share',
  collab: 'Collaborative groups',
  experiential: 'Experiential learning',
  inquiry: 'Inquiry',
  game: 'Gamification',
  reflect: 'Reflective practice'
};
const FORMATIVE = {
  oral: 'Oral questions',
  boards: 'Show-me boards',
  exit: 'Exit tickets',
  observe: 'Observation checklist',
  peer: 'Peer assessment',
  self: 'Self-assessment',
  quiz: 'Short quiz'
};
const PROGRAMMES = {
  science: 'General Science', arts: 'General Arts', business: 'Business', agric: 'Agricultural Science',
  homeec: 'Home Economics', visual: 'Visual Arts', technical: 'Technical', mixed: 'Mixed programmes'
};
const DAYS = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday'];
const MONTHS = ['January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December'];

const DEFAULTS = {
  subject: 'Core Mathematics', heading: '', school: '', teacher: '', className: '',
  term: '1', dates: '', weekStart: '', day1: '', day2: '', week: 'y1w01', boys: 24, girls: 22, dur1: 80, dur2: 80,
  programme: 'mixed', bandMode: 'manual', lastScore: '', ap: 30, p: 50, hp: 20, groupSize: 'auto', seating: 'movable', lang: '',
  needs: ['shy', 'gifted'], needCounts: {}, res: ['manila', 'maths_set', 'calculators', 'material', 'tape'],
  strat: ['problem', 'talk', 'collab', 'experiential', 'inquiry', 'reflect'],
  fa: ['oral', 'boards', 'exit', 'peer', 'self'], keyMode: 'class', keyMins: 40, homework: true,
  detail: 'standard', figs: true, notes1: '', notes2: '', ai: null
};

/* ----------------------------------------------------------- helpers */
const erf = x => { const t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * Math.abs(x)); const y = 1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-x * x); return x >= 0 ? y : -y; };
const cdf = (x, m, sd) => 0.5 * (1 + erf((x - m) / (sd * Math.SQRT2)));
function spread(total, G, sizes) {          // share `total` across G groups as evenly as possible, never above sizes[g]
  const out = new Array(G).fill(0); let left = total;
  for (let round = 0; left > 0 && round < 100; round++) {
    let moved = false;
    for (let g = 0; g < G && left > 0; g++) if (out[g] < sizes[g]) { out[g]++; left--; moved = true; }
    if (!moved) break;
  }
  return out;
}
function parseDate(v) { const m = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v || ''); return m ? new Date(+m[1], +m[2] - 1, +m[3]) : null; }
const fmtDate = d => `${DAYS[(d.getDay() + 6) % 7] || ''} ${d.getDate()} ${MONTHS[d.getMonth()]} ${d.getFullYear()}`.trim();

/* ----------------------------------------------------------- class context */
function context(s) {
  const boys = Math.max(0, Math.round(+s.boys || 0)), girls = Math.max(0, Math.round(+s.girls || 0));
  const n = Math.max(1, boys + girls);
  const needs = new Set(s.needs), res = new Set(s.res), strat = new Set(s.strat), fa = new Set(s.fa);
  const large = n >= 45;
  const auto = s.groupSize === 'auto' || !s.groupSize;
  let gs = auto ? (n <= 24 ? 4 : n <= 40 ? 5 : 6) : +s.groupSize;
  gs = Math.min(Math.max(gs, 3), 8);
  const G = Math.max(1, Math.round(n / gs));
  const lo = Math.floor(n / G), hi = Math.ceil(n / G);
  const size = lo === hi ? `${lo}` : `${lo}–${hi}`;
  // readiness: typed percentages, an estimate from the last test average, or unknown
  let mode = s.bandMode || 'manual';
  let pa = +s.ap || 0, pp = +s.p || 0, ph = +s.hp || 0, source = 'manual';
  const score = parseFloat(s.lastScore);
  if (mode === 'score' && score >= 0 && score <= 100) {
    pa = cdf(55, score, 15) * 100; ph = (1 - cdf(75, score, 15)) * 100; pp = 100 - pa - ph; source = 'score';
  } else if (mode === 'score') mode = 'unknown';
  const tot = pa + pp + ph || 1;
  const ap = Math.round(n * pa / tot), hp = Math.round(n * ph / tot);
  const p = Math.max(0, n - ap - hp);
  const single = boys === 0 ? 'girls' : girls === 0 ? 'boys' : null;
  const girlShare = girls / n;
  const per = (x) => { const a = Math.floor(x / G), b = Math.ceil(x / G); return a === b ? `${a}` : `${a}–${b}`; };
  const counts = s.needCounts || {};
  const ctx = {
    s, n, boys, girls, single, girlShare, large, gs, G, size, needs, res, strat, fa, autoGroups: auto,
    band: { ap, p, hp, known: mode !== 'unknown', source, score },
    apShare: ap / n, hpShare: hp / n,
    perGroup: { girls: per(girls), boys: per(boys), hp: per(hp), ap: per(ap) },
    prog: s.programme, progName: PROGRAMMES[s.programme] || 'Mixed programmes',
    lang: (s.lang || '').trim(), detail: s.detail, figs: !!s.figs,
    has: r => res.has(r), need: x => needs.has(x), st: x => strat.has(x), fm: x => fa.has(x),
    count: k => Math.max(0, Math.round(+counts[k] || 0)),
    movable: s.seating !== 'fixed'
  };
  ctx.apHeavy = mode !== 'unknown' && ctx.apShare >= 0.45;
  ctx.hpHeavy = mode !== 'unknown' && ctx.hpShare >= 0.3;
  ctx.many = (k, one, more) => { const c = ctx.count(k); return c ? `${c} ${c === 1 ? one : more}` : more; };
  ctx.groups = ctx.movable
    ? `${G} mixed-ability groups of ${size}`
    : `${G} bench groups of ${size} (two benches turn to face each other)`;
  ctx.cards = ctx.has('printer') ? 'printed number cards' : (ctx.has('manila') ? 'number cards cut from manila card' : 'number cards cut from used exercise-book covers');
  ctx.boards = ctx.has('slates') ? 'mini whiteboards' : 'jotters held up';
  ctx.show = (what) => ctx.has('projector') ? `project ${what}` : (ctx.has('manila') ? `display ${what} on a manila chart prepared before the lesson` : `draw ${what} on the board before the lesson`);
  ctx.Show = (what) => { const t = ctx.show(what); return t[0].toUpperCase() + t.slice(1); };
  ctx.numberLine = ctx.has('tape') ? 'a floor number line marked with masking tape or chalk' : 'a large number line drawn along the board';
  ctx.digital = ctx.has('internet') && (ctx.has('phones') || ctx.has('projector'));
  // dates of the two lessons
  const ws = parseDate(s.weekStart);
  if (ws) {
    const mon = new Date(ws); mon.setDate(ws.getDate() - ((ws.getDay() + 6) % 7));
    const fri = new Date(mon); fri.setDate(mon.getDate() + 4);
    ctx.weekRange = mon.getMonth() === fri.getMonth()
      ? `${mon.getDate()}–${fri.getDate()} ${MONTHS[fri.getMonth()]} ${fri.getFullYear()}`
      : `${mon.getDate()} ${MONTHS[mon.getMonth()]} – ${fri.getDate()} ${MONTHS[fri.getMonth()]} ${fri.getFullYear()}`;
    ctx.lessonDate = [s.day1, s.day2].map(d => { if (d === '' || d == null) return null; const x = new Date(mon); x.setDate(mon.getDate() + (+d)); return x; });
  } else ctx.lessonDate = [null, null];
  ctx.groupPlan = groupPlan(ctx);
  return ctx;
}

/* ----------------------------------------------------------- a concrete group plan */
function groupPlan(ctx) {
  const { G, n } = ctx;
  const sizes = Array.from({ length: G }, (_, g) => Math.floor(n / G) + (g < n % G ? 1 : 0));
  // girls (or boys) in a small minority sit at least two to a group, so nobody is the only girl (or boy) in a group
  let girls;
  const m = Math.min(ctx.girls, ctx.boys);
  if (!ctx.single && m < 2 * G) {
    const minority = new Array(G).fill(0), k = Math.floor(m / 2);
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) minority[Math.floor(i * G / Math.max(1, k))] += 2;
    if (m % 2) minority[minority.findIndex(x => x > 0) >= 0 ? minority.findIndex(x => x > 0) : 0] += 1;
    girls = ctx.girls <= ctx.boys ? minority : minority.map((x, g) => sizes[g] - x);
    ctx.paired = { who: ctx.girls <= ctx.boys ? 'girls' : 'boys', mixed: minority.filter(x => x > 0).length, groups: G };
  } else girls = spread(ctx.girls, G, sizes);
  const hp = spread(ctx.band.hp, G, sizes);
  // AP learners fill from the last group backwards, so the groups that got an extra HP learner do not also get an extra AP learner
  const ap = spread(ctx.band.ap, G, sizes.map((s, g) => s - hp[g]).reverse()).reverse();
  const rows = sizes.map((sz, g) => ({ g: g + 1, size: sz, girls: girls[g], boys: sz - girls[g], hp: hp[g], ap: Math.min(ap[g], sz - hp[g]), notes: [] }));
  rows.forEach(r => { r.p = Math.max(0, r.size - r.hp - r.ap); });
  // learners who must sit at the front go to the front groups, one or two per group
  const front = [['visual', 'low vision'], ['hearing', 'hearing impairment']];
  let g = 0;
  for (const [k, label] of front) {
    if (!ctx.need(k)) continue;
    const c = ctx.count(k) || 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < c; i++) { const r = rows[g % G]; r.notes.push(label); g++; }
  }
  if (ctx.need('physical')) { const c = ctx.count('physical') || 1; for (let i = 0; i < c; i++) rows[(G - 1 - i + G) % G].notes.push('physical disability (aisle seat, near the door)'); }
  if (ctx.need('attention')) { const c = ctx.count('attention') || 1; for (let i = 0; i < c; i++) rows[(Math.floor(G / 2) + i) % G].notes.push('attention difficulty (timekeeper role)'); }
  rows.forEach(r => { if (r.notes.some(x => /vision|hearing/.test(x))) r.front = true; });
  return rows;
}

/* ----------------------------------------------------------- lesson timing
   Every activity has a base time (for an 80-minute lesson), a minimum, a priority
   (1 = essential, 0 = carried over and must happen) and optionally `extra`
   (used only when there is spare time). */
function plan(phases, D, opts = {}) {
  const intro = Math.max(5, Math.round(D * 0.125 / 5) * 5), close = Math.max(5, Math.round(D * 0.125 / 5) * 5);
  const budgets = { intro, main: Math.max(10, D - intro - close), close };
  const out = {}, dropped = [];
  for (const ph of ['intro', 'main', 'close']) {
    const items = phases[ph].slice();
    const budget = budgets[ph];
    const chosen = [];
    let used = 0;
    const order = items.slice().sort((a, b) => (a.pri ?? 1) - (b.pri ?? 1));
    for (const it of order) {
      if (it.extra && !(D > 80 || (opts.hpHeavy && D >= 80 && used + (it.min || it.base) <= budget))) continue;
      if (used + (it.min || it.base) <= budget) { chosen.push(it); used += it.min || it.base; }
      else dropped.push({ ...it, ph });
    }
    chosen.sort((a, b) => items.indexOf(a) - items.indexOf(b));
    const sumBase = chosen.reduce((t, it) => t + it.base, 0) || 1;
    const unit = budget % 5 === 0 && chosen.every(it => (it.min || 0) % 5 === 0) && budget / 5 >= chosen.length ? 5 : 1;
    const mins = chosen.map(it => Math.max(it.min || 0, budget * it.base / sumBase));
    const units = mins.map(m => Math.floor(m / unit));
    let left = budget / unit - units.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
    const rema = mins.map((m, i) => [m / unit - units[i], i]).sort((a, b) => b[0] - a[0]);
    for (let k = 0; left > 0 && rema.length; k = (k + 1) % rema.length) { units[rema[k][1]]++; left--; }
    while (left < 0) { const i = units.indexOf(Math.max(...units)); units[i]--; left++; }
    out[ph] = { mins: budget, items: chosen.map((it, i) => ({ ...it, t: units[i] * unit })) };
  }
  out.dropped = dropped;
  return out;
}

/* ----------------------------------------------------------- build the planner */
function generate(settings) {
  const s = { ...DEFAULTS, ...settings };
  const W = WEEKS[s.week] || WEEKS[1];
  const AUTO_HEAD = ['', 'Learning Planner – Year One', 'Learning Planner – Year Two', 'Learning Planner – Year Three'];
  const ctx = context(s);
  const lessons = [];
  let carry = [];
  W.lessons.forEach((L, i) => {
    const D = Math.max(30, +(i === 0 ? s.dur1 : s.dur2) || 80);
    ctx.lessonNo = i + 1; ctx.D = D;
    const phases = L.phases(ctx);
    if (carry.length) phases.main = [...carry, ...phases.main];
    const timing = plan(phases, D, { hpHeavy: ctx.hpHeavy });
    // essential main activities that did not fit move to the next lesson, where they are planned for real
    const last = i === W.lessons.length - 1;
    carry = last ? [] : timing.dropped.filter(it => it.ph === 'main' && !it.extra && (it.pri ?? 1) <= 1)
      .map(it => ({ ...it, pri: 0, carried: i + 1, title: it.title.replace(/^Activity \d+ – /, 'Carried over: ') }));
    timing.carriedOut = carry.map(it => it.id);
    lessons.push({ L, D, timing, i });
  });
  lessons.forEach(x => { ctx.lessonNo = x.i + 1; ctx.D = x.D; x.blocks = renderLesson(x.L, x.timing, ctx, x.i + 1, s); });
  const d1 = lessons[0].D, d2 = lessons[1].D;
  const dur = d1 === d2 ? `2 lessons × ${d1} min` : `Lesson 1: ${d1} min; Lesson 2: ${d2} min`;
  const dates = ctx.weekRange || s.dates;
  const doc = {
    subject: s.subject || 'Core Mathematics',
    extra: [s.school && `School: ${s.school}`, s.teacher && `Teacher: ${s.teacher}`, s.term && `Semester ${s.term}`, dates && `Week of ${dates}`].filter(Boolean),
    heading: AUTO_HEAD.includes((s.heading || '').trim()) ? (W.heading || 'Learning Planner – Year One') : s.heading.trim(),
    year: W.year || 1,
    learners: ctx.single ? `${ctx.n} (all ${ctx.single})` : `${ctx.n} (Boys ${ctx.boys}, Girls ${ctx.girls})`,
    week: String(W.week), duration: dur, form: s.className ? s.className : String(W.year || 1), className: s.className || '',
    strand: [B.p(W.strand)], substrand: [B.p(W.substrand)], standard: [B.p(W.standard)],
    outcome: [B.p(W.outcome)], indicators: [B.ol(W.indicators)], eqs: [B.ol(W.eqs(ctx))],
    strategies: W.strategies(ctx), resources: W.resources(ctx),
    diff: W.differentiation(ctx, lessons),
    lessons: lessons.map((x, i) => {
      const dt = ctx.lessonDate[i];
      return { title: `Lesson ${i + 1}${dt ? ' · ' + fmtDate(dt) : ''} (${x.D} min): ${x.L.title}`, ref: x.L.ref, blocks: x.blocks, timing: x.timing };
    }),
    assessment: W.assessment(ctx), reflection: W.reflection(ctx),
    summary: { ctx, lessons, W, s }
  };
  if (s.ai && s.ai.diff && s.ai.diff.length) doc.diff.push(B.p('**Adaptations for this class (agreed with Claude)**', { before: 4, color: 'accent' }), B.ul(s.ai.diff.map(cleanText), { size: 9.5 }));
  return doc;
}

/* teacher text and Claude text: keep $…$ only when the maths reads cleanly, never break the markup */
function cleanText(t) {
  let x = String(t || '').replace(/\r/g, '').trim();
  const parts = x.split('$');
  if (parts.length % 2 === 0) x = x.replace(/\$/g, '');
  else x = x.replace(/\$([^$]+)\$/g, (m, tex) => (typeof TeX !== 'undefined' && TeX.parse(tex).errors.length) ? tex : m);
  return x;
}
const plainTeacher = t => String(t || '').replace(/\$/g, '＄').trim();

function renderLesson(L, timing, ctx, no, s) {
  const out = [];
  const names = { intro: 'Introduction', main: 'Main lesson', close: 'Closure' };
  const ai = (s.ai && s.ai.lessons && s.ai.lessons[no - 1]) || [];
  const used = new Set();
  const adaptFor = id => ai.filter((a, k) => { if (a.after === id && !used.has(k)) { used.add(k); return true; } return false; });
  for (const ph of ['intro', 'main', 'close']) {
    const P = timing[ph];
    out.push(B.h(`${names[ph]} (${P.mins} min)`, { rule: true, before: ph === 'intro' ? 2 : 8 }));
    for (const it of P.items) {
      const org = it.org ? (typeof it.org === 'function' ? it.org(ctx) : it.org) : '';
      out.push(B.bar(it.title, `${it.t} min${org ? ' · ' + org : ''}`, { before: 5 }));
      if (it.carried) out.push(B.note(`Planned here because Lesson ${it.carried} was too short for it.`, { size: 9 }));
      out.push(...pointify(it.body(ctx, it.t).filter(Boolean)));
      if (it.tiers) {
        const tr = it.tiers(ctx);
        const first = arr => Array.isArray(arr) ? (arr.find(x => typeof x === 'string' && x.trim()) || '') : '';
        // the AP task, then the support the teacher gives (a second AP line that is not another task)
        const apSupport = (tr.ap || []).slice(1).find(x => typeof x === 'string' && !/^\*\*(Quiz|Exercise|Theory)/.test(x));
        out.push(B.label('Differentiated practice'));
        out.push(B.ul([
          `**AP (supported):** ${first(tr.ap)}${apSupport ? ` — **Support:** ${apSupport}` : ''}`,
          `**P (core):** ${first(tr.p)}`,
          `**HP (challenge):** ${first(tr.hp)}`
        ], { size: 9.4 }));
      }
      const inc = it.inc ? Object.entries(it.inc).filter(([k]) => ctx.need(k)).map(([k, v]) => `**${INC_LABEL[k]}${ctx.count(k) ? ` (${ctx.count(k)})` : ''}:** ${typeof v === 'function' ? v(ctx) : v}`) : [];
      if (inc.length) out.push(B.label('Inclusion'), B.ul(inc, { size: 9.2 }));
      if (ctx.detail === 'detailed' && it.ask && it.ask.length) out.push(B.label('Key questions to ask'), B.ul(it.ask, { size: 9.2 }));
      for (const a of adaptFor(it.id)) out.push(B.adapt(`**Adaptation:** ${cleanText(a.text)}`, { size: 9.5 }));
    }
    for (const a of adaptFor(ph)) out.push(B.adapt(`**Adaptation:** ${cleanText(a.text)}`, { size: 9.5 }));
  }
  ai.forEach((a, k) => { if (!used.has(k)) out.push(B.adapt(`**Adaptation:** ${cleanText(a.text)}`, { size: 9.5 })); });
  const note = s['notes' + no];
  if (note && note.trim()) out.push(B.p(`**Teacher’s note:** ${plainTeacher(note)}`, { before: 4 }));
  if (timing.dropped.length) {
    const msgs = timing.dropped.map(it => {
      if (timing.carriedOut.includes(it.id)) return `${it.title.replace(/ \(.*\)$/, '')} did not fit, so it is planned at the start of Lesson ${no + 1}’s main lesson.`;
      return it.drop || `${it.title} is left out; use it in the next lesson.`;
    });
    out.push(B.note(`**Time note (${ctx.D}-minute lesson):** ` + msgs.join(' '), { size: 9 }));
  }
  return out;
}
/* point by point: running paragraphs become bullet points; a list that explains a point becomes its sub-list.
   Labels, notes, adaptations and paragraphs marked plain (Problem, Answer …) stay as they are. */
function pointify(list) {
  const out = []; let acc = null;
  const flush = () => { if (acc) { out.push(B.ul(acc.items, acc.size ? { size: acc.size } : {})); acc = null; } };
  for (const b of list) {
    if (!b) continue;
    if (b.k === 'p' && !b.label && !b.note && !b.adapt && !b.plain && !b.act) {
      const sz = b.size || 0;
      if (acc && acc.size !== sz) flush();
      if (!acc) acc = { items: [], size: sz };
      acc.items.push(String(b.text).trim().replace(/:$/, '.').replace(/\.\.$/, '.'));
      continue;
    }
    if ((b.k === 'ul' || b.k === 'ol') && acc && !b.sub) { const head = acc.items[acc.items.length - 1]; if (head) acc.items[acc.items.length - 1] = head.replace(/\.$/, ':'); flush(); out.push({ ...b, sub: true }); continue; }
    flush(); out.push(b);
  }
  flush();
  return out;
}
const INC_LABEL = {
  visual: 'Low vision', hearing: 'Hearing impairment', physical: 'Physical disability', reading: 'Reading difficulty',
  attention: 'Attention difficulty', language: 'Second-language learners', shy: 'Shy learners', gifted: 'Gifted learners',
  absent: 'Absentees', behaviour: 'Focus and behaviour'
};

    ref: `Teacher Manual: Year One, Section 1, Week 1, Focal Areas 1–2 (the subsets of ℝ; rational and irrational numbers). ${lm} Week 1: Notes “What is a number system?”, “The number sets”, “Rational and irrational decimals”; Worked Examples 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.7; Quiz 1, 2, 3, 6, 7; Exercise 1, 2, 6; Theory 2.`,
    phases: ctx => ({

            B.p(r`Explain the dot notation: a dot above a digit shows that it repeats; dots above the first and last digits of a block show that the whole block repeats. Then compare $\pi=3.14159265\ldots$ and $\sqrt{2}=1.41421356\ldots$: their decimals **never end and never repeat**${c.has('calculators') ? ', and a calculator shows only an approximation' : ''}.`),
            B.p(r`**Conclusion (learners write it):** the decimal of a rational number terminates or recurs; the decimal of an irrational number does neither.`),
            B.p(r`**Diamond nine (Teacher Manual strategy):** each group arranges nine cards in a diamond, “certainly terminates” at the top and “never ends, never repeats” at the bottom: $\dfrac{3}{8}$, $0.6$, $25\%$, $\dfrac{1}{3}$, $\dfrac{4}{11}$, $0.\dot{2}\dot{7}$, $\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{11}$, $\pi$. Groups justify the order to the class.`)
          ],
          tiers: c => ({
            ap: [r`Divide $\dfrac{3}{8}$ and $\dfrac{1}{3}$ using a long-division frame on the board; say which terminates.`],
            p: [r`Divide all three fractions; for $\dfrac{4}{11}$ name the repeating block and write it with dots: $0.\dot{3}\dot{6}$.`],
            hp: [r`Quiz 9: explain why a decimal that never ends and never repeats cannot be a fraction, and why $\pi\approx3.14$ is only an approximation.`]
          }),
          inc: {
            visual: 'Read each decimal aloud digit by digit (“nought point three six, three six, recurring”).',
            attention: 'One division at a time; tick each one off on the board.'
          },
          ask: [r`How can you tell from the decimal that $\dfrac{4}{11}$ is rational?`]
        },
        {
          id: 'a4', ind: [2], title: 'Activity 4 – Recurring decimals as fractions (Worked Examples 1.2 and 1.3)', base: 13, min: 10, pri: 1, org: 'teacher models, then readiness groups',
          drop: 'Activity 4 (Worked Examples 1.2 and 1.3) is taught at the start of Lesson 2; set Exercise 6 as homework.',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`**Model Worked Example 1.2** (a bank calculation gives $0.363636\ldots$):`),
            B.ol([
              r`Let $x=0.363636\ldots$ The repeating block, $36$, has two digits.`,
              r`Multiply by $100$: $100x=36.363636\ldots$`,
              r`Subtract; the repeating parts cancel: $100x-x=36$, so $99x=36$.`,
              r`$x=\dfrac{36}{99}=\dfrac{4}{11}$ (divide by $9$).`
            ]),
            B.p(r`**Method (key box):** let $x$ equal the decimal, multiply by a power of 10 so that the repeating parts line up, then subtract.`),
            c.apHeavy ? B.p(r`**Extra modelling (about ${c.band.ap} AP learners):** do the key-box example $x=0.\dot{3}$ first (“we do”), then let pairs try $0.555\ldots$ before Worked Example 1.2 is repeated by a learner at the board.`) : null,
            B.p(r`**Worked Example 1.3** (P and HP): $x=0.1666\ldots$; $10x=1.666\ldots$; $100x=16.666\ldots$; $100x-10x=90x=15$, so $x=\dfrac{15}{90}=\dfrac{1}{6}$. Check: $1\div6=0.1666\ldots$`)
          ],
          tiers: c => ({
            ap: [r`Key box: $x=0.\dot{3}$, $10x=3.333\ldots$, $9x=3$, $x=\dfrac{1}{3}$.`, r`Quiz 3 with the steps as gap-fill: $0.4545\ldots=\dfrac{45}{99}=\dfrac{5}{11}$.`],
            p: [r`Exercise 1: $0.0625=\dfrac{625}{10000}=\dfrac{1}{16}$.`, r`Exercise 6: $0.\dot{1}\dot{5}=\dfrac{15}{99}=\dfrac{5}{33}$.`],
            hp: [r`Quiz 6: $0.0777\ldots=\dfrac{7}{90}$.`, r`Theory 2: $0.\dot{2}\dot{7}=\dfrac{3}{11}$ and $0.58\dot{3}=\dfrac{525}{900}=\dfrac{7}{12}$.`]
          }),
          inc: {
            reading: 'Give the steps of Worked Example 1.2 as a printed or copied model to follow line by line.',
            attention: 'Break the method into four numbered steps on the board; the learner ticks each step.',
            gifted: 'Ask why the method works: what must be true of the two lines before you subtract?'
          },
          ask: ['Why multiply by 100 and not by 10 for $0.3636\\ldots$?']
        },
        {
          id: 'x1', title: 'Extension – Worked Example 1.7 with the whole class', base: 10, min: 10, pri: 3, extra: true, org: 'whole class',
          body: c => [B.p(r`Is $\sqrt{72}$ rational because $72$ is an integer? $72=36\times2$, so $\sqrt{72}=\sqrt{36}\times\sqrt{2}=6\sqrt{2}$. If $6\sqrt{2}$ were rational, dividing by $6$ would make $\sqrt{2}$ rational, which it is not. Learners then try Exercise 5: $\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$.`)]
        }
      ],
      close: [
        {
          id: 'recap', title: ctx.st('game') ? 'Recap: team quiz' : 'Recap', base: 4, min: 3, pri: 2, org: 'whole class',
          drop: 'The recap questions (Quiz 1, 2 and 7) are asked orally while learners hand in the exit ticket.',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`${c.st('game') ? 'Groups score a point for each correct board answer. ' : ''}Quiz 1: the smallest set containing $-9$ (integers). Quiz 2: which is irrational, $\sqrt{121}$, $0.125$, $\sqrt{15}$ or $-\dfrac{11}{7}$? ($\sqrt{15}$). Quiz 7: a whole number that is not natural ($0$).`)
          ]
        },
        {
          id: 'exit1', exit: true, title: 'Exit ticket', base: 6, min: 4, pri: 1, org: 'individual',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`**Exercise 2:** place each number in its smallest set: $-\sqrt{49}$, $\sqrt{50}$, $0.\dot{0}\dot{9}$, $125\%$, $-8$, $0$.`),
            B.p(r`**Answers:** $-\sqrt{49}=-7\in\mathbb{Z}$; $\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}$ irrational; $0.\dot{0}\dot{9}=\dfrac{1}{11}\in\mathbb{Q}$; $125\%=\dfrac{5}{4}\in\mathbb{Q}$; $-8\in\mathbb{Z}$; $0\in W$. Sort the tickets into AP, P and HP piles to regroup for Lesson 2.`, { size: 9 }),
            c.s.homework ? B.p(r`**Homework:** Theory 1 (smallest set for $-12$, $0$, $\dfrac{7}{4}$, $\sqrt{36}$, $\sqrt{10}$, and one real-life use of negative numbers).`) : null
          ].filter(Boolean)
        }
      ]
    })
  };

  /* ===================================================================== LESSON 2 */
  const L2 = {
    title: 'Closure, ordering real numbers, and real numbers in daily life',
    ref: `Teacher Manual: Year One, Section 1, Week 1, Focal Area 1 (the closure property) and Focal Area 2 (applications). ${lm} Week 1: Notes “Closure”, “Ordering numbers on the number line”, “Real numbers in daily life and a famous proof”; Worked Examples 1.4 and 1.5; Quiz 4, 5, 8, 9, 10; Exercise 3, 4, 5, 7, 8; Theory 3 and 5.`,
    phases: ctx => ({
      intro: [
        {
          id: 'review', title: 'Review of homework and exit tickets', base: 4, min: 3, pri: 2, org: 'whole class',
          body: c => [B.p(r`Two learners present Theory 1: $\mathbb{Z}$: $-12$; $W$: $0$; $\mathbb{Q}$: $\dfrac{7}{4}$; $\mathbb{N}$: $\sqrt{36}=6$; irrational: $\sqrt{10}$. Clear up the errors seen on the exit tickets (for example, thinking $0$ is natural or that $\sqrt{50}$ is rational).`)],
          drop: 'Return the exit tickets with written comments instead of the oral review.'
        },
        {
          id: 'puzzle', title: 'Starter: Is the club right? (Worked Example 1.4)', base: 6, min: 4, pri: 1, org: 'whole class vote',
          body: c => [B.p(r`Write the claim: “The whole numbers are closed under subtraction because $9-3=6$ is a whole number.” Learners vote${c.has('slates') ? ' on mini whiteboards' : ' with a show of hands'}: true or false? Leave the question open until Activity 1.`)],
          inc: { shy: 'Secret vote on jotters first, so every learner commits to an answer.' }
        }
      ],
      main: [
        {
          id: 'b1', ind: [1], title: 'Activity 1 – Closure investigation', base: 25, min: 15, pri: 1, org: c => c.groups,
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`**Definition (Notes):** a set $S$ is **closed** under an operation if, whenever $a$ and $b$ are in $S$, the result is also in $S$, for **every** pair. One example that works does not prove closure; one **counterexample** disproves it: $2-5=-3\notin\mathbb{N}$ and $1\div2=\dfrac{1}{2}\notin\mathbb{N}$.`),
            B.p(r`**Resolve Worked Example 1.4:** try the pair $3$ and $9$: $3-9=-6$, which is not a whole number, so the claim is false.`),
            B.p(r`Groups copy and complete the closure table, writing an example for each “Yes” and a counterexample for each “No”. Compare with the table in the Notes:`),
            B.table({
              cols: [20, 20, 20, 20, 20], fill: 'F2CEED', small: true,
              head: ['Set', '$+$', '$-$', '$\\times$', r`$\div$ (divisor $\neq0$)`],
              rows: [['$\\mathbb{N}$', 'Yes', 'No', 'Yes', 'No'], ['$W$', 'Yes', 'No', 'Yes', 'No'], ['$\\mathbb{Z}$', 'Yes', 'Yes', 'Yes', 'No'], ['$\\mathbb{Q}$', 'Yes', 'Yes', 'Yes', 'Yes'], ['$\\mathbb{R}$', 'Yes', 'Yes', 'Yes', 'Yes']]
            }),
            B.p(r`**Warning:** division by $0$ is undefined. Say “$\mathbb{Q}$ is closed under division by a **non-zero** rational number”, never simply “closed under division”.`),
            c.apHeavy ? B.p(r`**Extra modelling (about ${c.band.ap} AP learners):** fill the $\mathbb{N}$ row together first, saying each test aloud (“$2-5=-3$; is $-3$ a natural number? No, so not closed”), then the groups continue.`) : null
          ].filter(Boolean),
          tiers: c => ({
            ap: [r`Table with rows $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$ started; prompts “Try $2-5$”, “Try $1\div2$”.`, r`Quiz 4: which statement about $\mathbb{Z}$ is true? (closed under subtraction)`],
            p: [r`Complete the whole table with a counterexample for every “No”.`, r`Exercise 3: two counterexamples showing $\mathbb{Z}$ is not closed under division, e.g. $1\div2=\dfrac{1}{2}$, $7\div3=\dfrac{7}{3}$.`],
            hp: [r`Are the irrational numbers closed under $+$ and $\times$? $\sqrt{2}+(-\sqrt{2})=0$ and $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}=2$ (also Quiz 8: $\sqrt{5}\times\sqrt{5}=5$), so no.`, r`Theory 3: explain the difference between checking a claim with one example and disproving it.`]
          }),
          inc: {
            visual: 'Give the table in large print; read each row aloud as the group fills it.',
            hearing: 'Write “example” and “counterexample” with one instance of each on the board.',
            reading: 'Table cells need only a calculation and Yes/No; read the definition aloud.',
            attention: 'Give the learner one row of the table to own and report.',
            language: c => 'Sentence frame: “___ is not closed under ___ because ___”' + lang(c) + '.',
            gifted: 'HP column: the irrational numbers and Theory 3.',
            shy: 'The recorder role lets a quiet learner contribute in writing before reporting.',
            behaviour: 'Each group member owns one operation column, so everyone has a task.'
          },
          ask: ['Why is one counterexample enough?', 'Why must we say “non-zero” for division?']
        },
        {
          id: 'b2', ind: [2], title: 'Activity 2 – Ordering numbers and absolute value (Worked Example 1.5)', base: 20, min: 10, pri: 1, org: 'whole class, then pairs',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`Using ${c.numberLine}: numbers increase from left to right; among negatives the one nearer to zero is greater, $-2>-7$. The **absolute value** $|x|$ is the distance of $x$ from $0$: $|-6|=6$, $|4|=4$. To compare surds use bounds: $1.4<\sqrt{2}<1.5$ because $1.4^2=1.96<2<2.25=1.5^2$.`),
            B.p(r`**Worked Example 1.5:** five learners hold the cards $-2.3$, $-\dfrac{7}{4}$, $0$, $\sqrt{2}$ and $1.3$ (°C) and the class arranges them in ascending order. Steps: $-\dfrac{7}{4}=-1.75$; $\sqrt{2}\approx1.414$; $-2.3<-1.75$ because $-2.3$ is further left; $1.3<\sqrt{2}$ because $1.3^2=1.69<2$.`),
            B.p(r`**Answer:** $-2.3<-\dfrac{7}{4}<0<1.3<\sqrt{2}$`),
            B.p(r`**Construct $\sqrt{2}$ on the number line (Teacher Manual: right-angled triangles):** draw a square of side $1$ on the segment from $0$ to $1$; by Pythagoras its diagonal is $\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$ (Notes). ${c.has('maths_set') ? 'With compasses' : 'With a string of the same length'} centred at $0$, swing the diagonal down onto the line: it lands at $\sqrt{2}\approx1.414$, just to the right of $1.3$.`),
            c.apHeavy ? B.p(r`**Extra modelling:** change every number to a decimal on the board first ($-2.3$, $-1.75$, $0$, $1.3$, $1.414$), then order the decimals.`) : null,
            c.figs ? B.fig('w01-numberline', r`Figure 2. The numbers of Worked Example 1.5 in order on the number line.`, 10) : null,
            c.digital ? B.p(r`Optional check: plot the five numbers on a GeoGebra number line.`) : null
          ].filter(Boolean),
          tiers: c => ({
            ap: [r`Place $-7$, $-2$, $0$, $|-6|$ and $|4|$ on the number line.`, r`Quiz 10: $|-7|-|3-8|=7-5=2$.`],
            p: [r`Exercise 7: $-\sqrt{3}<-1.6<1.7<\sqrt{3}<\dfrac{7}{4}$ (since $\sqrt{3}\approx1.732$).`, r`Exercise 8: $|-12|-|5-9|+|-3|=12-4+3=11$.`],
            hp: [r`Theory 5: order $-\sqrt{4}$, $-1.75$, $0$, $\dfrac{4}{3}$, $\sqrt{3}$ with reasons: $-\sqrt{4}<-1.75<0<\dfrac{4}{3}<\sqrt{3}$.`, r`Wheel of Theodorus: on the $\sqrt{2}$ diagonal draw a right angle and a side of $1$ to construct $\sqrt{3}$.`]
          }),
          inc: {
            visual: c => c.has('tactile') ? 'Tactile number line: knots on a string at each whole number; the learner places beads.' : 'A large, high-contrast number line at the front; describe each position aloud.',
            physical: 'The learner orders the cards on a desk or directs a partner where to stand.',
            hearing: 'Point to each position as you say it; write the inequalities on the board.',
            attention: 'Give the learner a number card to hold in the human number line.',
            shy: 'Shy learners may hold cards in the human number line without speaking; partners talk first.'
          },
          ask: ['Which is greater, $-2.3$ or $-1.75$? How do you know?']
        },
        {
          id: 'b3', ind: [1, 2], title: 'Activity 3 – Real numbers in daily life', base: 15, min: 10, pri: 2, org: c => c.groups,
          drop: 'Activity 3 (daily life) becomes homework: Exercise 4 and one example from the learners’ own programme.',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`From the Notes: counting chairs needs $\mathbb{N}$ or $W$; profit and loss need $\mathbb{Z}$; a measured length such as $2.75$ m is rational; the circumference $2\pi r$ of a circle with rational radius $r\neq0$ is irrational. On a thermometer, $-5$ is an integer while $18.5=\dfrac{37}{2}$ is rational but not an integer.`),
            B.p(r`**Exercise 4 (problem):** a diver starts at $-18$ m and rises $7.5$ m. New position: $-18+7.5=-10.5$ m, a rational number that is not an integer.`),
            B.p(r`**Group task (${c.progName} context):** classify each quantity and report in one minute.`),
            B.table({
              cols: [62, 38], fill: 'F2CEED', head: ['Quantity', 'Number and set'],
              rows: ctxList(c).map(([a, b]) => [a, b])
            })
          ],
          tiers: c => ({
            ap: [r`Classify the four quantities in the table.`],
            p: [r`Add two quantities of your own from your programme and classify them.`],
            hp: [r`**Enrichment (Notes):** why $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational (proof by contradiction).`, r`Exercise 5: $\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.`]
          }),
          inc: {
            language: c => 'Allow reporting with real objects or drawings' + lang(c) + '.',
            gifted: 'Lead the √2 proof and present it to the class if time allows.'
          }
        },
        {
          id: 'x2', title: 'Extension – Why √2 is irrational', base: 10, min: 10, pri: 3, extra: true, org: 'whole class',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`Suppose $\sqrt{2}=\dfrac{p}{q}$ in lowest terms. Then $p^2=2q^2$, so $p$ is even; write $p=2k$. Then $4k^2=2q^2$, so $q^2=2k^2$ and $q$ is even too. Both share the factor 2, which contradicts “lowest terms”, so $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.`)
          ]
        }
      ],
      close: [
        {
          id: 'check', title: ctx.fm('self') ? 'Self-assessment checklist' : 'Summary', base: 4, min: 3, pri: 2, org: 'individual',
          body: c => [B.p(c.fm('self')
            ? r`Learners mark each statement of the ${lm} checklist green, amber or red: I can name the five number sets; explain why one number can belong to several sets; decide whether a decimal is rational or irrational; change a recurring decimal into a fraction; test a closure claim with a counterexample; order real numbers and use absolute value.`
            : r`Learners state the key facts: $\mathbb{N}\subset W\subset\mathbb{Z}\subset\mathbb{Q}\subset\mathbb{R}$; a set is closed only if the result stays in the set for every pair; $|x|\ge0$.`)],
          drop: 'Set the Learner Material checklist as homework.'
        },
        {
          id: 'exit2', exit: true, title: 'Exit ticket', base: 6, min: 4, pri: 1, org: 'individual',
          body: c => [
            B.p(r`**Quiz 5:** which list is in ascending order? ($-\dfrac{3}{2},\ -1.3,\ 0,\ \sqrt{2}$). **Quiz 9:** a decimal that never ends and never repeats represents … (an irrational number).`),
            c.s.homework ? B.p(r`**Homework:** Theory 4: show that $\sqrt{98}=7\sqrt{2}$ is irrational; read ahead to Week 2 (Properties of Operations and Sets).`) : B.p('Preview Week 2: Properties of Operations and Sets.')
          ]
        }
      ]
    })
  };

  /* ===================================================================== WEEK */
  WEEKS[1] = WEEKS.y1w01 = {
    id: 'y1w01', year: 1, week: 1, title: 'The Real Number System', heading: 'Learning Planner – Year One',
    meta: { label: 'Year 1, Week 1', title: 'The Real Number System', family: 'number', nEx: 7, exLabel: i => `Worked Example 1.${i + 1}`, flags: [], handmade: true, section: 'Number Sets' },
    strand: 'Number for Everyday Life',
    substrand: 'Real Number and Numeration System (RNNS)',
    standard: 'Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the real number system and the operations of the various subsets of real numbers.',
    outcome: 'Apply the relationship and differences between the sets of rational and irrational numbers, and use them to solve problems.',
    indicators: [
      'Develop the real number system using the closure property.',
      'Distinguish between rational and irrational numbers by converting common fractions to decimals, and solve related problems.'
    ],
    eqs: ctx => [
      'Why do we need different kinds of numbers, and how do the number sets fit inside one another?',
      'How does the decimal form of a number tell us whether it is rational or irrational?',
      'How can one counterexample show that a set is not closed under an operation?',
      r`How do we compare and order real numbers, including surds such as $\sqrt{2}$?`
    ],
    lessons: [L1, L2],

    strategies: ctx => {
      const S = {
